claimBoundary: The matrix separates source-observed runtime evidence from inferences and unavailable recording claims. It does not authorize copying competitor expression.

rows.lifecycleState: intact → sharp contact → cut → halves separate → fall/settle
rows.observed: two cut halves and cap facts are present, but the +value and earnings banner are emitted on the cut event before the visible separation/settle lifecycle completes
rows.inference: reward ownership is screen-space/event-first instead of object-local/post-settle
rows.acceptance: cut, separation, settle, local reward and cumulative sync are independently observable in both viewports

rows.lifecycleState: airborne → blunt contact → bounce/recovery or sharp contact → anchored
rows.observed: collision taxonomy exists in state and tests, while supports render as a largely shared box language with no strong route-role/value affordance
rows.inference: the player must recall metadata or HUD text to distinguish main, branch and recovery surfaces
rows.acceptance: contact result, route role and recovery affordance are visible at natural play distance without relying on helper copy

rows.lifecycleState: spawned → approach window → contact → failed → replay
rows.observed: mobile-natural-zero fails on a spike at 8.67s after four cuts before reaching the finish wall; sibling timing can win
rows.inference: hazard readability and default-route fairness are not closed by a sibling natural pass
rows.acceptance: default mobile natural run exposes a pre-warning/escape and reaches the declared terminal or remains an explicit blocked QA case

rows.lifecycleState: approach → aggregate wall contact → contact reveal → reward reveal → celebration → terminal
rows.observed: aggregate collision/clamp and staged phases exist; labels are fixed to the viewport, terminal overlay can cover the wall, and the x4/x2/x0.5 operation is applied to score rather than totalEarnings
rows.inference: the wall is implemented as a collision/settlement system but not yet as a single world-owned decision/reward object
rows.acceptance: continuous wall, world-local labels, no knife penetration for every knife part, lane-specific risk, selected-brick reveal, and one authoritative final reward

rows.lifecycleState: failed or won → terminal overlay → replay/next action
rows.observed: terminal copy says a light tap restarts, but onPointerDown ignores failed/won and only the small replay button restarts; overlay obscures arena context
rows.inference: copy, input affordance and recovery hierarchy disagree
rows.acceptance: one explicit, visible replay action matches copy, preserves cause context, and does not hide an unread finish reveal

rows.rendererPresentationPath: index.html/src/main.ts vs poc-3d.html/src/poc-3d.ts; build.ts vs build-3d.ts; qa:browser vs qa:3d
rows.observed: the two entrypoints are confirmed historical variants of the same game, but still have different assets, UI, build outputs and QA coverage; qa:3d success is not proof of the default game journey
rows.inference: without targetGame/entrypoint/version fingerprints, evidence from different development stages can be mixed even when the display title lineage is valid
rows.acceptance: all reports and screenshots include targetGame, workspace, entrypoint and build-output/version fingerprints; POC evidence remains explicitly non-release for the main journey

rows.lifecycleState: pointer down → held/released; visible → hidden → resumed; active → terminal
rows.rendererPresentationPath: shell pointer handlers + ActionInput + fixed-step accumulator + requestAnimationFrame loop
rows.observed: release is shell-scoped, no visibility/blur lifecycle is wired, finish reveal still leaves status ready for act(), and RAF keeps rendering after terminal
rows.inference: app-switch, drag-out or reveal-time taps can create non-player-authored state changes and extra work
rows.acceptance: pointer capture/cancel, hidden-tab pause, finish-phase input lock and terminal render throttle are covered by natural tests
